item.title: Blowouts, quince curls, and 27 years of miracles at Margarita’s Hair Design - Chicago Reader
item.description: For nearly three decades, Duarte’s Avondale shop is more than a hair salon: It has remained an oasis for the immigrant community.

item.title: One TRiiBE, divided? - Chicago Reader
item.description: After two terminations and a public Instagram dispute, the last two eligible employees at Chicago’s celebrated Black-owned newsroom, The Triibe, head to a union vote on March 25.

item.title: Local witch-house artist Häxa welcomes spring at Reggies Music Joint - Chicago Reader
item.description: Eerie, evocative, and skewed—that's the style and vibe of Heather Häxa’s work.

item.title: Acoustic guitarist Gwenifer Raymond plays sci-fi-themed fingerstyle blues at escape velocity - Chicago Reader
item.description: Though Raymond was raised in Wales and presently lives in Brighton, England, her acoustic fingerpicking adorns the weighty sonorities of American country blues with melodic elaboration that draws on a broader array of influences, instrumental and otherwise.

item.title: Reader Bites: The trippy vibe at Chocolate Shoppe Ice Cream - Chicago Reader
item.description: We were about to enter the twilight zone, complete with terrifying characters, a spinning disco ball, and 48 rich flavors to choose from.

item.title: Filter Photo’s annual survey show - Chicago Reader
item.description: In “Context 2026,” Filter Photo’s annual survey of contemporary photography, 25 artists investigate the hidden narrative behind still images.

item.title: Evanston faith leaders slam Chicago real estate firm for contracting with ICE
item.description: Interfaith clergy and immigrant rights advocates announce a national campaign targeting Highlands REIT, which plans to lease a private prison facility in Colorado to ICE.

item.title: El ultimo sueño de Frida y Diego is a fanciful take on a well-worn story - Chicago Reader
item.description: Lyric's staging of a new opera about Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera offers an original and challenging score, but also sags a bit dramatically.

item.title: Unwritten - Chicago Reader
item.description: Abdulrahman Hamdi’s paintings appear to be full of text, but their communicative ability is strictly wordless.

item.title: Power plays - Chicago Reader
item.description: The paintings of Berenice Vargas Bravo mix socialist realism, surrealistic juxtaposition, and pop sensibility.
